applicable_when: The kernel is severely underutilized on all fronts (Memory SOL 5.63%, Compute SOL 6.77%, 0.46 waves/SM). The root cause is twofold: (1) the grid of 980 blocks on 132 SMs leaves ~54% of SMs idle during the single partial wave, and (2) the output store pattern `out_ptr0 + (x0 + 528*x1)` scatters writes across rows with stride 528 while only 64 elements per row are written, causing L1TEX stalls that account for 51.1% of all stall cycles (13.1 cycles avg per stall). Prior XBLOCK autotune attempts all failed correctness because they changed XBLOCK without correctly recomputing the grid. The fix is to restructure the kernel as a 2D tiled kernel: one program dimension covers the 64-element column axis (XBLOCK_COL tiles of 64), and another covers the row/batch axis (XBLOCK_ROW tiles). This makes stores within each CTA contiguous in the column dimension (x0 is the fast axis in the output), improving coalescing, and allows the grid to scale to fill all 132 SMs.
